reply_channel.recorded: An event callback. Replies (DA1/DA2, DSR/CPR, DECRQM, XTGETTCAP, Kitty acks and a=q answers) are sent as RioEvent::PtyWrite(route_id, String) through EventListener::send_event. Window-size reports arrive as TextAreaSizeRequest, OSC colour queries as ColorRequest and OSC 52 reads as ClipboardLoad, each carrying a formatter closure the embedder applies before writing. kitty_graphics.recorded: Broad, inside the crate. Transmission: t=d with chunking, t=f, t=t (path must contain tty-graphics-protocol; deleted after reading), t=s (shm_open on Unix, a file mapping on Windows). Formats: f=8, f=16, f=24, f=32 raw and f=100 PNG; PNG decodes only with the non-default `graphics` feature, otherwise EINVAL. o=z zlib with a decompressed-size cap. Placement: a=T and a=p at the cursor with x/y/w/h source rectangle, c/r cell span, X/Y sub-cell offset, C=1, z index. U=1 virtual placements are stored as metadata and ansi/kitty_virtual.rs supplies the placeholder decoders, but scanning cells for U+10EEEE and compositing is the embedder's renderer's job. Deletes: a/A, i/I, n/N, c/C, p/P, x/X, y/Y, z/Z, q/Q, r/R. a=q runs the real load path and answers OK or the error, honouring q=. Limits: 320 MiB image store per terminal with eviction of unreferenced images; 10000 px per axis and 400 MiB payload at parse; 4096x4096 display cap. Not implemented: animation (a=f, a=a, a=c answered EINVAL:unsupported action) and relative placements (P/Q/H/V parsed, never used).

Text written over a Sixel/iTerm2 picture splits it into cropped children. Quota: total_limit 320 MiB per terminal, evicting images not in use.

damage_tracking.recorded: yes — the render state keeps a global dirty state (FALSE / PARTIAL / FULL) and a per-row dirty flag; the embedder clears both with ghostty_render_state_clean after drawing a frame. Kitty graphics add storage and per-image generation stamps.
damage_tracking.quoted: The render state API keeps track of dirty state at two independent layers: a global dirty state that indicates whether the entire frame is clean, partially dirty, or fully dirty, and a per-row dirty state that allows tracking which rows in a partially dirty frame have changed.

state_snapshot.recorded: Yes, two routes. (1) Binary snapshot: ghostty_snapshot_encode / _encode_buf / _encode_alloc and ghostty_snapshot_decoder_new / _ready / _next / _decode — 'GHOSTSNP' v1, CRC32C-framed records, a READY marker after the active screens and the unfinished VT-parser continuation, then history pages newest-first so a client can render before scrollback arrives. Format v1 is WIP with no compatibility guarantee; the C API landed 2026-08-03, so it is absent from crate 0.2.1 and present on libghostty-rs master. (2) VT formatter: ghostty_formatter_terminal_new with GHOSTTY_FORMATTER_FORMAT_VT re-encodes the screen as VT bytes with optional extras (cursor, SGR, OSC 8, protection, kitty keyboard, charsets, palette, modes, scrolling region, tabstops, pwd) — the route zmx takes through the Zig API. Neither route carries Kitty image or placement state.
state_snapshot.quoted: A snapshot is an ordered, CRC-protected record stream. Its READY marker follows enough state to render and resume the terminal, including any unfinished VT parser input. Older scrollback pages follow READY and the FINISH marker terminates the complete snapshot.

threading_and_loop.recorded: The embedder owns the read loop: libghostty-vt has no PTY layer, no event loop, no timer and no background thread; bytes go in through ghostty_terminal_vt_write, and every effect callback runs synchronously on the calling thread (no re-entrant vt_write). The C API has no internal locking; the render docs expect a lock held across render-state update. The Rust bindings make every type !Send and !Sync, so a terminal lives on one thread and talks through channels.
threading_and_loop.quoted: In particular, all libghostty-vt types are !Send, meaning they cannot be transferred across threads, since the C API is allowed to use thread-local state; they are also !Sync, meaning they cannot be shared across threads, since data races may occur as the C API is not guarded with mutexes or other synchronization mechanisms.

reply_channel.recorded: A per-terminal WRITE_PTY callback receives every reply byte string (DSR, DECRQM, mode 2048 size reports, Kitty graphics a=q and transmit responses). DA1/DA2/DA3, XTWINOPS size, XTVERSION, ENQ and colour-scheme queries are answered by embedder callbacks that return data for the terminal to encode. With no WRITE_PTY installed, reply-producing sequences are silently dropped — so a window replica that installs none, next to a host that installs one, gives exactly-once replies by construction.
reply_channel.quoted: Feeds raw bytes through the terminal's VT stream parser, updating terminal state accordingly. By default, sequences that require output (queries, device status reports) are silently ignored. Use ghostty_terminal_set() with GHOSTTY_TERMINAL_OPT_WRITE_PTY to install a callback that receives response data.

kitty_graphics.recorded: Full core implementation behind the C API (build feature kitty_graphics, on by default). Actions q, t, T, p, d, f, a, c. Media: direct, file, temporary file, shared memory (file/temp/shm are opt-in per terminal; temp is restricted to a directory the embedder names). Formats: RGB (24), RGBA (32), PNG (100) — PNG only if the embedder installs a decode callback, otherwise rejected. zlib compression (o=z), inflated before storage. Placements: direct (anchored to tracked page-list pins), virtual (U=1) and relative (P/Q parent chains). Deletes a, i, n, c, f, p, q, r, x, y, z with upper-case freeing variants. Query and transmit replies go out through the WRITE_PTY callback. z-index with BELOW_BG / BELOW_TEXT / ABOVE_TEXT iterator filters. Animation frames (a=f, a=a, a=c) composed eagerly into RGBA; the current frame is exposed, but timed playback is driven by the Ghostty app renderer (ImageStorage.animationTick) and has no C API entry point, so an embedder sees client-driven frame changes only. Storage quota per screen (0 disables) and a 65 MiB APC buffer cap. Read side: GhosttyKittyGraphics handle, placement iterator with layer filter, image lookup returning decoded pixels plus generation stamps, and render_info geometry. Unicode placeholders: the API reports is_virtual and a per-row KITTY_VIRTUAL_PLACEHOLDER flag, but position/rect calls return NO_VALUE for virtual placements, so the embedder must decode U+10EEEE cells (diacritics, fg-colour image id) itself.
kitty_graphics.quoted: Before images can be stored, Kitty graphics must be enabled on the terminal by setting a non-zero storage limit with GHOSTTY_TERMINAL_OPT_KITTY_IMAGE_STORAGE_LIMIT, and a PNG decoder callback must be installed via ghostty_sys_set() with GHOSTTY_SYS_OPT_DECODE_PNG.

picture_anchoring.recorded: Tracked pin: each direct placement's location is a *PageList.Pin tracked by the page list, so scrolling, scrollback pruning and resize/reflow move it with the text. Virtual placements anchor through placeholder cells in the grid; relative placements resolve through the parent chain at render time. Quota: storage limit per screen (320 MB default inside the Zig storage struct; C API terminals must set a non-zero limit, 0 disables and deletes everything), plus a 65 MiB APC buffer cap for Kitty payloads.
picture_anchoring.quoted: Converts the placement's internal pin to viewport-relative column and row coordinates. The returned coordinates represent the top-left corner of the placement in the viewport's grid coordinate space.

state_snapshot.recorded: No, not for pictures. TD's gridwire::encode_snapshot re-encodes only alacritty's grid as VT bytes. libghostty-vt's own binary snapshot (C API added upstream on 2026-08-03, after crate 0.2.1's pin) says Kitty image and placement state is not part of it. So a re-attaching window would get text and no pictures unless TD ships image bytes and placements itself. The window's replica also cannot re-parse t=t or t=s transmissions, because the protocol makes the first terminal that reads them, the host's shadow, delete the file or unlink the shared memory.

threading_and_loop.recorded: The loop is split. alacritty's EventLoop owns the PTY reader thread and parser, and TD's host.rs TeeReader already copies every read on that thread while holding the lease. libghostty-vt owns no loop, thread or PTY: the embedder calls vt_write. Its Rust handles are !Send + !Sync, so the shadow Terminal must live on one thread. It can be created lazily on alacritty's reader thread (e.g. thread-local per pane) and fed inside TeeReader::read before alacritty parses the chunk. The alternative is a dedicated thread fed through a channel, which loses the ordering that both the attach fence and the a=q reply depend on.
threading_and_loop.quoted: Handle types (`Terminal`, `RenderState`, `KeyEncoder`, etc.) are `!Send + !Sync` by design. Callers should drive all operations from a single thread.

reply_channel.recorded: There are two reply channels, and TD must merge them by hand. alacritty emits Event::PtyWrite(String), which TD bounces to the PTY. libghostty-vt calls its write_pty callback (Rust: Terminal::on_pty_write) for every reply it generates, DA and DSR included. To keep 'exactly once', TD must drop every libghostty reply except Kitty APC responses (ESC _ G ...). Ordering matters as well. kitty's detection recipe is a=q followed by DA1, and a terminal that answers DA1 first is judged to lack pictures. So the shadow must parse each chunk, and write its a=q answer, before alacritty answers a DA1 in the same chunk; viu and kitten icat both send a=q and then CSI c in the captures.
reply_channel.quoted: To check if a terminal emulator supports the graphics protocol the best way is to send the above *query action* followed by a request for the `primary device attributes <https://vt100.net/docs/vt510-rm/DA1.html>`_. If you get back an answer for the device attributes without getting back an answer for the *query action* the terminal emulator does not support the graphics protocol.

kitty_graphics.recorded: All of it comes from libghostty-vt; alacritty contributes nothing, because vte 0.15 swallows APC. At the crates.io 0.2.1 pin (ghostty a887df4) libghostty-vt covers: transmission t=d/f/t/s, where f, t and s are off by default in the library build and TD must enable each one; formats f=24/32/100, where PNG works only with a TD-supplied decoder callback; zlib compression (o=z); direct placements (a=T/a=p) held on tracked pins and virtual U=1 placements; deletes a/i/n/c/f/p/q/r/x/y/z; a=q query replies; and z-index layers exposed as BELOW_BG/BELOW_TEXT/ABOVE_TEXT. Animation (a=f/a/c) returns 'ERROR: unimplemented action' at this pin. Upstream added animation on 2026-08-21 and relative placements (P/Q) on 2026-08-20, both after the pin. Quota: 10 MB by default in the library build, set by the embedder.

picture_anchoring.recorded: Tracked pins in libghostty's own page list: a direct placement's location is `pin: *PageList.Pin`, which moves with scrolling and reflow in libghostty's grid, not alacritty's. TD would map libghostty viewport rows onto alacritty viewport rows one to one, which holds only while the two grids stay in lockstep; scrollback caps also differ (alacritty counts lines, libghostty counts bytes). label: zmx — server-side snapshots with libghostty-vt (host/replica prior art)

grid_api.recorded: zmx never iterates cells itself. It uses libghostty-vt's Zig API: ghostty_vt.Terminal.init(io, gpa, {cols, rows, max_scrollback_lines, max_scrollback_bytes}); term.vtStream() and vt_stream.nextSlice(bytes) to feed PTY output; term.resize(gpa, {cols, rows}); term.modes.get/set; term.screens.active.pages with getTopLeft(.screen/.active) and pin(.{.active = .{x, y}}) to bound scrollback and viewport; ghostty_vt.Selection.init(tl, br, false); ghostty_vt.formatter.TerminalFormatter.init(term, .vt) with .content and .extra; term.getTitle(), term.getPwd(), term.colors (dynamic fg/bg/cursor); term.screens.active.cursor for logging; ghostty_vt.Parser for input classification.

damage_tracking.recorded: no — zmx neither reads nor reports damage: each PTY read is forwarded raw to every client and the whole screen is re-serialized only when a client re-attaches.

state_snapshot.recorded: yes — util.serializeTerminalState(alloc, term) re-encodes the server's libghostty-vt Terminal as VT bytes with ghostty's TerminalFormatter(.vt) and sends them as one Output message, on re-attach only (not first attach): phase 1 = scrollback as styled text with no extras, then CSI 2J / CSI H / SGR 0; phase 2 = the active screen with modes, scroll region, Kitty keyboard and modifyOtherKeys, cursor, charsets and protection; then OSC 7 cwd, OSC 2 title and OSC 10/11/12 dynamic colours. Not carried: palette, tabstops (deliberately), DECSET 2026 (deliberately stripped), per-cell OSC 8 links, the primary screen under an alt screen, and every picture. Against TD's gridwire::encode_snapshot: same strategy (re-emit the grid as VT bytes for a stock emulator), but zmx also carries scroll region, charsets, title, cwd and dynamic colours, which TD does not; both lose the primary grid beneath an alt screen; ghostty's formatter emits modes BEFORE content, where TD restores modes last on purpose; and zmx has no replica emulator on the client and no equivalent of TD's grid_hash check. libghostty-vt also has a binary snapshot API (ghostty_snapshot_*) that zmx does not use.

threading_and_loop.recorded: zmx owns the whole loop: one double-forked daemon process per session, holding the PTY it created with forkpty(); a single-threaded poll(2) loop over the server socket, the PTY master, a signal pipe and each client socket; every PTY read (up to 4096 bytes) is fed to the libghostty-vt stream and broadcast to clients in the same iteration, so there are no threads, no locks and no snapshot/stream seam to fence. Clients are also single-threaded poll(2) loops that pipe stdin to the socket and Output to stdout.
threading_and_loop.quoted:
- The `daemon` and client processes communicate via a unix socket
- Both `daemon` and `client` loops leverage `poll(2)`
- Each session creates its own unix socket file
- We restore terminal state and output using `libghostty-vt`

reply_channel.recorded: Two regimes. With no terminal client attached, zmx itself scans PTY output for DA1/DA2 queries and queues fixed answers (ESC[?62;22c, ESC[>1;10;0c) into the PTY write buffer; nothing else is answered, because the server's libghostty-vt stream is readonly and ignores queries (Kitty a=q, DSR, XTVERSION go unanswered). With clients attached, queries reach every client's own terminal raw, and only the leader client's input — which carries its terminal's replies — is forwarded to the PTY; a non-leader's input is dropped unless it looks like typing (which makes it leader), so each reply is written once.

kitty_graphics.recorded: None restored, passthrough live. While a client is attached, every PTY read is broadcast raw to it, so Kitty APC reaches the client's own terminal and draws there if that terminal supports it (pixel sizes are forwarded in the winsize since 0.7.0). The server-side libghostty-vt Terminal parses the APC with the readonly stream (kitty_graphics on by default, 10 MB lib quota, direct medium only, PNG disabled without a decode_png hook, which zmx does not set), but zmx never renders or replays those images: the TerminalFormatter it uses for the re-attach snapshot emits no Kitty images, so pictures vanish on re-attach (issue #14, open since 2025-12-04). With no client attached, a=q queries go unanswered.
kitty_graphics.quoted:
`ghostty-vt.TerminalFormatter` does *not* currently support kitty protocol images: https://github.com/ghostty-org/ghostty/blob/08c9661683edc1e9e63d8e6abd469a68faaee575/src/terminal/formatter.zig#L457

This is what we use to print a snapshot of the terminal to `zmx` clients.

picture_anchoring.recorded: n/a — zmx anchors no pictures. Live pictures are anchored by the client's own terminal and are lost on re-attach; the server-side libghostty-vt tracks Kitty placements with its own grid pins but zmx never replays them. Server-side storage quota is libghostty's embedded default of 10 MB per session terminal (zmx's initTerminal does not override it).

integration_path.recorded: not a library (reference only) — zmx builds a single executable and exports no module or C API; TD could borrow its design (and, being MIT, its code), or run panes inside zmx sessions as a process substrate, but not link it.

api_stability.recorded: Pre-1.0 application (0.8.1) with no library API to be stable; the README says it has not reached a stable state, an IPC change between versions kills running sessions, and the CHANGELOG marks *BREAKING* changes in 0.1.0, 0.5.0 and 0.7.0. It pins libghostty-vt to a dev commit, whose own snapshot format is declared work-in-progress.
